manifest.sha256: 64 lowercase hex characters: the SHA-256 of the file's exact bytes
manifest.size: the file's byte length, an integer from 0 to 9007199254740991 (2^53 - 1, the largest integer every JSON client reads exactly)
manifest.same_digest_same_size: two entries with the same sha256 must have the same size
manifest.not_in_manifest: upload state, latest pointer, authors, comments, timestamps, URLs, S3 keys and sync binding metadata

canonical_encoding.files_order: ascending by the UTF-8 bytes of path (not UTF-16 code units: JavaScript's default sort differs above U+FFFF)
canonical_encoding.object_keys: sorted; every key is ASCII, so byte, code-point and UTF-16 order agree
canonical_encoding.whitespace: none outside strings: separators are ',' and ':'
canonical_encoding.strings: UTF-8; only '"' and '\' are escaped, because policy-valid paths contain no control characters or lone surrogates
canonical_encoding.numbers: integers in decimal with no sign, fraction or exponent
canonical_encoding.manifest_sha256: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical bytes

unicode.assigned_only: every code point must be assigned in Unicode 15.1; unassigned and future code points are refused
unicode.normalization: every path must already be NFC
unicode.comparison_key: NFC(full_casefold(NFC(segment))), with default full case folding (CaseFolding.txt status C and F)

path.reserved_segment_match: full match against each segment's comparison key, so CON, Con.txt and nul.tar.gz are all reserved

checks.rule: the path is not the empty string
no C0 or C1 control character, DEL, lone surrogate or forbidden character
every code point is assigned in Unicode 15.1
the path equals its NFC form
each segment is at most max_segment_bytes UTF-8 bytes
no segment ends in '.' or ' ' (Windows strips them)
a first segment whose comparison key equals a canonical_spelling_roots entry is spelled exactly like it, and an allowed rule that matches the folded path also matches the path as spelled
the first rule matching the folded path does not have server_action 'reject'

path.check_order: checks run in the order listed; the first failing check names the error

matching.syntax: each rule's regex must match the whole path (Python re.fullmatch, JavaScript ^(?:regex)$ with the 's' and 'u' flags)
matching.subject: the folded path: every segment replaced by its comparison key, joined with '/'
matching.case: rule regexes are written in lowercase, because they are matched against the case-folded path

client_actions.wait_then_exclude: wait for the writer to finish (the reserved sibling may be incomplete), then leave the marker out

matching.rule_order: every rule that rejects at any depth comes before the first allow rule, so a credential, environment file, package-manager config, VCS or dependency directory, agent state, build cache or OS metadata inside an allowed .hyperframes subtree stays out

rules.basis: Process lock held by the media writer, not project content
Media id reservation: the sibling asset may still be incomplete, so capture waits for the writer to finish
Generated media metadata that the project does not use for preview or rendering
Unfinished or abandoned writes at any depth: core's atomic-write temp <file>.hfXXXXXX.tmp, *.tmp, *.part, editor *.swp and *~
Render work directories at any depth (frames, often GBs): core RENDER_TEMP_DIR (packages/core/src/projectFolders.ts) plus distributed assembly's <output>.assemble-work-XXXXXX
Agent and IDE state at any depth; Desktop vendors .claude/skills into every project and regenerates it
Version control and installed dependencies at any depth
Build tool caches at any depth
Credentials: .env, every .env.* (templates included: real keys land there and no reader needs them) and .envrc, at any depth
May hold registry tokens, and nothing in a HyperFrames project reads them; stripping credentials would change the bytes
Credential files by name at any depth. *.key is deliberately absent: Keynote decks are plausible project sources
Operating-system metadata: it changes when a folder is browsed and would show as false edits and conflicts
Completed transcripts, keyed by media hash; costly to regenerate
Transcription (ASR) preferences, not run state; Desktop's Duplicate copies it with the transcripts
The project's brand kit selection is authored, portable project content
Studio edits read at render and preview time; without them a pulled project renders differently
Authored input to the caption build; rebuilding captions needs it
Desktop's podcast camera and recorder transcodes (media/, proxies/), which the page plays by this path and a receiving client cannot regenerate without the original files; a dotfile there stays out
External bindings and sync receipts: share and review links (review files carry the owner's email), the CLI publish id and deploy stacks. A copy must start unbound, so these never travel

Known client state: comments, chat and run logs; machine pointers, locks and caches; personal data (photo and voice copies) and account-bound job state, podcast job state included; studio preview caches under prepared-assets/ other than the podcast media above
Reserved client state area: only the named portable files above travel
Caches and render or snapshot output at the project root
Web build and test-coverage output at the project root, which the CLI publish leaves out and render never reads (build/ and outputs/ travel, because the publish ships them)
Authoring scratch at the project root: a Remotion port's source and the moment working copies with their references, none of which preview or render reads
Third-party reference video, large and re-downloadable

Authored source and config (index.html, compositions/, scenes/, assets/, hyperframes.json, meta.json, project.json, package.json, lockfiles, .hyperframesignore, .gitignore), portable briefs, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, completed .media assets with unused alternatives, .media/index.md, .media/preferences.json and .media/CREDITS.md, build/ and outputs/, and any unknown regular file outside a reserved area

client_notes.project_json: Root project.json is portable project content and is included. It is not sync identity: the owner workspace, composition, base snapshot, revision and receipts live outside the inventory, never in project.json.
client_notes.capture_preconditions: Do not capture while .hyperframes/history-turn.json exists (an agent turn is open) or while .hyperframes/project.lock is held.
client_notes.render_outputs: Leave out every path listed in .hyperframes/render-outputs.json: render outputs written outside renders/ are recorded there, and the server cannot know them.
client_notes.complete_capture: A file the client cannot read fails the capture; it never becomes a deletion. The exclusions above and the symlinks client_symlinks skips are the only files left out.
client_notes.symlinks: Symlinks and special files fail the capture, listing them; they are neither followed nor skipped, except the symlinks client_symlinks skips.
client_notes.empty_directories: Empty directories are not represented. Pull never deletes a local empty directory.

client_prefilter.rule: skip a file whose last segment is one of these before running any path check; macOS writes 'Icon\r' for a folder with a custom icon, and the carriage return would otherwise fail the whole capture with path_invalid_character

client_symlinks.match: a symlink whose folded path (each segment replaced by its comparison key, as for rules) starts with a listed prefix, at any depth below it
client_symlinks.rule: skip such a symlink instead of failing the capture, and on Pull leave such a local symlink in place as local state; a regular file under the prefix is captured like any other, and every other symlink or special file fails the capture
client_symlinks.basis: Desktop's podcast intake links the original camera files, which live outside the project, under assets/podcast/, and the page plays the transcodes under .hyperframes/prepared-assets/podcast/; real files there, such as the joins under assets/podcast/joins/, travel normally

stored_manifest.rule: Only stored snapshot reads use the v3 agent-state rule to retain immutable manifest digests. New captures and uploads use the current rules. Clients never install excluded paths; the server never signs their download URLs.
